slides.headline: For two centuries, one princely state ruled itself. Then, at noon, it stopped.
Hyderabad's accession to India
slides.body: At noon on September 17, 1948, the Nizam of Hyderabad broadcast a ceasefire and accession announcement, ending 'Operation Polo' - what Sardar Patel officially termed a 'Police Action' to avoid international intervention.

slides.headline: A 212,000 sq km state, folded in within days.
slides.body: The campaign, led by Major General J.N. Chaudhari, began September 13, 1948, following an economic blockade and destabilization attempts against the state. Four days later, it was over.

slides.eyebrow: Why it matters for Viksit Bharat 2047
slides.headline: Still marked as a liberation day, regionally, every year.
slides.body: The date is commemorated as Marathwada Liberation Day in Maharashtra and Hyderabad-Karnataka Liberation Day in Karnataka - a reminder that integrating a country isn't one clean signature, it's dozens of separate, sometimes contested, endings.
